newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania troops, police on alert as new protests loom.
newsitem.headline: Albania troops, police on alert as new protests loom.

text.p: Tens of thousands of irate Albanians, facing the loss of their life savings in pyramid investment schemes, took to the streets of Europe's poorest nation again on Sunday to demand state refunds.
Troops were out guarding state buildings in Berat after the town hall was set ablaze on Saturday, witnesses said.
In the capital Tirana about 30,000 people were seen gathering near the Selman Stermasi soccer stadium for a rally organised by the opposition Socialists.

In a televised address to the Balkan nation, embattled Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi promised his government would start paying back investors' deposits at the get-rich-quick pyramid schemes from February onwards.

"With the preparations made so far we may start the systematic distribution of the money from about February 5," Meksi said, adding the government already had a stockpile of 30 billion leks ($300 million) from two pyramid schemes.
But the pledge did little to quell restive Albanians, many of whom have lost all they have in schemes that offered high returns on relatively small deposits.
Albanian President Sali Berisha has urged calm, but opposition Socialists have vowed to press ahead with protests.

"We shall overthrow the government today at all costs," one protester at the Tirana stadium said, adding that there were rumours that the ruling Democratic party used money from pyramid schemes to fund their election campaign last summer.
Police in Tirana were on alert and officers massed behind the stadium where the rally kicked off at 11 a.m. (1000 GMT).
Road blocks were set up on routes into the capital, witnesses said.
Angry crowds set fire to government buildings in the southern towns of Lushnje and Berat on Saturday and state television reported disturbances in six other towns.
A crowd of about 5,000 people roughed up Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu, the Democratic Party chairman, in Lushnje, 80 km (55 miles) south of Tirana, on Saturday.
Lushnje was calm on Sunday morning. "People are peacefully demonstrating in the streets today," a witness said.
In the town of Berat, 120 km (80 miles) the army was out in force guarding state institutions, witnesses said.
"Army troops were seen guarding the state institutions which were not burned last night," a witness said, adding people had started gathering in the centre.
Thousands were also reported to be gathering in the southern town of Vlore, 150 km (100 miles) from Tirana.
Last week the crowd broke windows of the town hall after the Gjallica investement scheme, which offered 11 percent a month, failed to pay up after two weeks of suspended trade.
